name: Shlla'at
description: Shlla'at is a Sudanese fishing card game in which players capture cards from the table and from opponents' capture piles. A turn continues with a new draw after each capture until no capture is made. The Arabic name means 'uprooted'.

rules.objective: Capture cards from the table pool and from opponents' capture piles by matching rank (or with Joker/Ace for special capture). Score points for captured cards; first to reach the agreed target score wins.
rules.gameplay: Each player is dealt four cards; four cards are dealt face up to the centre as the pool; the rest form the stock. On your turn, draw one from the stock (when it has cards), then play one card. A normal card captures any available cards of the same rank from the pool or the top set of any opponent's capture pile. A Joker captures all cards of any one rank you choose; an Ace does the same unless the set is protected by a Joker. If you capture, draw again and play again until you play a card that captures nothing; then your turn ends. When the stock is empty, each player plays only one card per turn. The last player to have made a capture takes any remaining table cards. At end of hand, add the point value of your capture pile to your score; first to reach the agreed target (e.g. 500) wins.
